answer: Each epoch, tasks are graded by a panel of agents sampled randomly from a rotating pool, so an attacker never knows in advance which identities will judge; the panel works like a prism, splitting each submission across independent verifiers. To bias outcomes, an attacker must forge credibility across many nodes and harbor them long enough to be drawn together on one panel, paying registration stakes, uptime, and honest task fees that exceed any single-round payoff, making collusion economically irrational before it ever converges.
